bibl.title: GTDB: an ongoing census of bacterial and archaeal diversity through a phylogenetically consistent, rank normalized and complete genome-based taxonomy

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: A SPECIES BOUNDARY WHOSE JUSTIFICATION WAS TESTED, DISPROVED AND KEPT ON PURPOSE - the 95-96% average nucleotide identity threshold, defended in the literature by a claimed genetic discontinuity that this paper looks for in its own 254,090 genomes and does not find
span.quote: We demonstrate the lack of such a discontinuity by considering the ANI between closest pairs of representative genomes from GTDB species within the same genus (Figure 4A ). If a meaningful discontinuity existed, we would expect to find few such pairs with an ANI between 83% and 95% supporting the idea of discrete, well-separated species boundaries. In contrast, we find nearly equal numbers of pairs with ANI values between 78% and 95%. The addition of non-representative genomes can only increase the likelihood of there being genomes with ANI values between 83% and 95% to a species representative and thus a genetic continuum between species.

span.label: whether prokaryotic species are discrete enough for a similarity threshold to be a natural boundary, and how to keep a genome-based taxonomy stable while it grows by 270% and its ranks are set by two continuous statistics
span.quote: An ANI threshold of 95–96% is widely considered the ‘gold standard’ for quantitatively delineating species ( 27–30 ) and it has recently been proposed that a genetic discontinuity exists between 83% and 95% ANI which would further support the use of ANI for defining species boundaries ( 31 , 32 ). This genetic discontinuity has also been observed between genomes recovered from specific environments such as the human gut and soil ( 33 ).

span.label: a rank-normalised genome taxonomy in which higher ranks are delineated by relative evolutionary divergence and species by ANI, with a published policy for names, a quantitative rule for replacing type genomes, and a measurement showing the species threshold has no natural discontinuity behind it
span.quote: In order to taxonomically organise this large and growing genome dataset, the GTDB uses relative evolutionary divergence (RED) to delineate higher-rank taxa and average nucleotide identity (ANI) to delineate species clusters ( 4 , 5 ). Use of these quantitative criteria for circumscribing taxa allows for automated classification of new genomes ( 6 ), ensures all genomes are classified from species to domain, and normalizes the definition of taxonomic ranks across the bacterial and archaeal domains.

span.label: method
span.quote: We conclude with a discussion on the use of average nucleotide identities as a pragmatic approach for delineating prokaryotic species.

span.label: prokaryotic diversity as a continuum, most of it never cultured and most of it unnamed, being cut into named classes so that it can be talked about at all
span.quote: The use of ANI to delineate species despite the lack of clear evidence for discrete species boundaries in the GTDB dataset is a pragmatic approach for organizing the rapidly growing biodiversity being discovered with metagenomic approaches ( 2 , 3 , 15 ). Leaving this diversity unclassified would severely limit the ability to effectively communicate scientific results as exemplified by 28.5% of genomes at NCBI lacking a species classification and 77.0% of GTDB R06-RS202 species clusters having an alphanumeric placeholder name.

span.label: a taxonomy rebuilt each release from the NCBI Assembly database, with ANI and alignment fraction to a single representative genome deciding species membership and a Balanced ANI Score deciding when a representative may be replaced
span.term: a taxonomy rebuilt each release from the NCBI Assembly database, with ANI and alignment fraction to a single representative genome deciding species membership and a Balanced ANI Score deciding when a representative may be replaced
span.quote: Each GTDB species cluster is defined by a single representative genome and species assignments are established by considering the ANI and AF (alignment fraction) of genomes to these representatives as previously described ( 5 ).

span.label: **THE JUSTIFICATION FOR THE SPECIES THRESHOLD WAS TESTED AND FAILED**: `An ANI threshold of 95-96% is widely considered the `GOLD STANDARD` ... and it has recently been proposed that A GENETIC DISCONTINUITY EXISTS BETWEEN 83% AND 95% ANI WHICH WOULD FURTHER SUPPORT THE USE OF ANI for defining species boundaries.` Re-tested here: `IF A MEANINGFUL DISCONTINUITY EXISTED, WE WOULD EXPECT TO FIND FEW SUCH PAIRS with an ANI between 83% and 95% ... IN CONTRAST, WE FIND NEARLY EQUAL NUMBERS OF PAIRS WITH ANI VALUES BETWEEN 78% AND 95%.` **The gap the line was supposed to sit inside is not there**
span.quote: We demonstrate the lack of such a discontinuity by considering the ANI between closest pairs of representative genomes from GTDB species within the same genus (Figure 4A ). If a meaningful discontinuity existed, we would expect to find few such pairs with an ANI between 83% and 95% supporting the idea of discrete, well-separated species boundaries. In contrast, we find nearly equal numbers of pairs with ANI values between 78% and 95%. The addition of non-representative genomes can only increase the likelihood of there being genomes with ANI values between 83% and 95% to a species representative and thus a genetic continuum between species.

span.label: **AND THE THRESHOLD IS KEPT, WITH THE REASON WRITTEN DOWN**: `The use of ANI to delineate species DESPITE THE LACK OF CLEAR EVIDENCE FOR DISCRETE SPECIES BOUNDARIES in the GTDB dataset IS A PRAGMATIC APPROACH for organizing the rapidly growing biodiversity ... LEAVING THIS DIVERSITY UNCLASSIFIED WOULD SEVERELY LIMIT THE ABILITY TO EFFECTIVELY COMMUNICATE SCIENTIFIC RESULTS.` **Read against simonneau2018 in the same corpus - `THIS DEFINITION IS, THEREFORE, NO LONGER ARBITRARY, BUT BASED ON A SCIENTIFIC APPROACH`. One field says it has removed the arbitrariness; this one measures for a natural boundary, does not find it, and keeps the rule anyway**
span.quote: The use of ANI to delineate species despite the lack of clear evidence for discrete species boundaries in the GTDB dataset is a pragmatic approach for organizing the rapidly growing biodiversity being discovered with metagenomic approaches ( 2 , 3 , 15 ). Leaving this diversity unclassified would severely limit the ability to effectively communicate scientific results as exemplified by 28.5% of genomes at NCBI lacking a species classification and 77.0% of GTDB R06-RS202 species clusters having an alphanumeric placeholder name.

span.label: AND THE ARGUMENT FOR DOING SO IS QUOTED FROM SOMEBODY ELSE, IN FULL: `What we want from a species definition is A SET OF EASILY APPLIED AND STABLE RULES by which to decide WHEN TWO ORGANISMS ARE SIMILAR ENOUGH ... TO BE GIVEN THE SAME NAME. The needs for such a guide to taxonomic practice in medicine, biotechnology and defense are obvious, and EVEN ARBITRARY RULES TO SATISFY THEM WOULD BE BETTER THAN NO RULES AT ALL.` **The clearest statement in the corpus that a definition can be justified by its usefulness rather than by nature** - and it is a quotation, not this paper's own sentence
span.quote: Doolittle and Papke ( 37 ) best articulate the rationale for a pragmatic species definition: ‘What we want from a species definition is a set of easily applied and stable rules by which to decide when two organisms are similar enough in their genomic and/or phenotypic properties to be given the same name. The needs for such a guide to taxonomic practice in medicine, biotechnology and defense are obvious, and even arbitrary rules to satisfy them would be better than no rules at all.’

span.label: **AND THE RANKS ARE NORMALISED BY A CONTINUOUS STATISTIC**: `the GTDB uses RELATIVE EVOLUTIONARY DIVERGENCE (RED) TO DELINEATE HIGHER-RANK TAXA AND AVERAGE NUCLEOTIDE IDENTITY (ANI) TO DELINEATE SPECIES CLUSTERS. Use of these QUANTITATIVE CRITERIA FOR CIRCUMSCRIBING TAXA allows for automated classification ..., ensures ALL GENOMES ARE CLASSIFIED FROM SPECIES TO DOMAIN, and NORMALIZES THE DEFINITION OF TAXONOMIC RANKS across the bacterial and archaeal domains.` **A genus in one phylum and a genus in another are made comparable by a number** - which is the thing traditional taxonomy could never guarantee
span.quote: In order to taxonomically organise this large and growing genome dataset, the GTDB uses relative evolutionary divergence (RED) to delineate higher-rank taxa and average nucleotide identity (ANI) to delineate species clusters ( 4 , 5 ). Use of these quantitative criteria for circumscribing taxa allows for automated classification of new genomes ( 6 ), ensures all genomes are classified from species to domain, and normalizes the definition of taxonomic ranks across the bacterial and archaeal domains.

span.label: AND STABILITY IS ENFORCED BY A SCORE WITH AN EXPLICIT ASYMMETRY: `representatives SHOULD ONLY BE REPLACED BY EQUIVALENT ASSEMBLIES OF DEMONSTRABLY HIGHER QUALITY ... quantitatively defined by the BALANCED ANI SCORE (BAS) which is 0.5 x (ANI score) + 0.5 x (quality score) ... AN EXISTING REPRESENTATIVE IS ONLY REPLACED ... IF IT HAS A BAS >= 10 ABOVE the BAS of the current representative. This achieves the goal of TAXONOMIC STABILITY BY REQUIRING A NEW REPRESENTATIVE TO BE OF INCREASINGLY HIGHER QUALITY THE MORE DISSIMILAR IT IS from the current representative.` **The cost of changing what a name points at rises with how much the pointing would move**
span.quote: GTDB representatives are updated according to two primary principles: (i) representatives should be assembled from the type strain of a species whenever possible, and (ii) representatives should only be replaced by equivalent assemblies of demonstrably higher quality (Figure 3B ). These two principles are quantitatively defined by the Balanced ANI Score (BAS) which is 0.5 × (ANI score) + 0.5 × (quality score), where the ANI score is 100 – 20 × (100 – ANI to current representative) and the quality score is defined by the criteria given in Table 1 . An existing representative is only replaced by a new or updated genome if it has a BAS ≥ 10 above the BAS of the current representative. This achieves the goal of taxonomic stability by requiring a new representative to be of increasingly higher quality (as defined by the quality score) the more dissimilar it is from the current representative (as defined by the ANI score).

span.label: AND A NAME CAN TURN OUT TO HAVE POINTED AT THE WRONG ORGANISM: `GCF_004359525.2 IS ASSEMBLED FROM THE TYPE STRAIN OF Macrococcus equipercicus WHILE GCF_004359515.1 IS ASSEMBLED FROM THE TYPE STRAIN OF M. carouselicus, indicating that prior to the ... assembly being updated, AN M. CAROUSELICUS STRAIN WAS ERRONEOUSLY CONSIDERED AS THE TYPE STRAIN FOR M. EQUIPERCICUS at NCBI and in the GTDB.` **For at least one release a species cluster carried one name and contained the other organism**, and the correction came from an assembly update rather than from biology
span.quote: This discrepancy can be explained by the fact that GCF_004359525.2 is assembled from the type strain of Macrococcus equipercicus while GCF_004359515.1 is assembled from the type strain of M. carouselicus indicating that prior to the GCF_004359525.1 assembly being updated, an M. carouselicus strain was erroneously considered as the type strain for M. equipercicus at NCBI and in the GTDB. While the exception, such large-scale reassignments and assembly errors do occur and we make a best effort to identify and handle all such cases.

span.label: **AND MOST OF THE TAXONOMY HAS NO NAME AND NO ORGANISM**: `28.5% OF GENOMES AT NCBI LACKING A SPECIES CLASSIFICATION and 77.0% OF GTDB R06-RS202 SPECIES CLUSTERS HAVING AN ALPHANUMERIC PLACEHOLDER NAME`; and `OVER 70% OF ARCHAEAL SPECIES, GENERA, FAMILIES, AND ORDERS LACKING AN AVAILABLE CULTURED REPRESENTATIVE`. **Three quarters of the species in a species database are named by a string like CG2-30-70-394**, and half the taxa exist only as assembled sequence
span.quote: Unlike the number of bacterial genomes, MAGs account for the majority of taxonomic diversity covered by GTDB R06-RS202 (Figure 1E and F ; Supplementary Table S1 ). Over 50% of bacterial taxa, regardless of rank, consist exclusively of MAGs and/or SAGs despite MAGs (50 669 genomes) and SAGs (745 genomes) representing only 20.2% of the 254 090 bacterial genomes. Similarly, nearly 50% of all archaeal taxa, regardless of rank, consist exclusively of MAGs and/or SAGs with over 70% of archaeal species, genera, families, and orders lacking an available cultured representative (Figure 1F ).

span.label: AND THE NAMING POLICY IS FIVE RULES ABOUT WHO MAY NAME WHAT: Latin names are `NO LONGER PROPOSED BY GTDB CURATORS UNLESS THERE IS AN ASSOCIATED PUBLICATION WITH TAXON DESCRIPTIONS`; names above genus `WITHOUT DESIGNATED TYPE MATERIAL ... WILL NO LONGER BE INCORPORATED`; `LATIN NAMES IN PREPRINTS ARE ALSO NO LONGER INCORPORATED ... AS NAMES CAN CHANGE BETWEEN PREPRINT AND PEER-REVIEWED PUBLICATION`; and placeholder names are never swapped for other placeholder names, `EVEN WHEN [THEY] ARE UNWIELDY, e.g. CG2-30-70-394 WHICH IS USED AS A GENUS, FAMILY, ORDER, CLASS AND PHYLUM NAME`. **Continuity of reference beats readability, explicitly**
span.quote: Finally, to preserve name continuity, we do not replace alphanumeric placeholder names with other placeholder names, even when names (mostly introduced in early releases) are unwieldy, e.g. CG2-30-70-394 which is used as a genus, family, order, class and phylum name.

span.label: AND A DEFINITIONAL PARAMETER IS ABOUT TO MOVE BECAUSE OF DATA QUALITY: `we expect to CHANGE THE AF CRITERIA used for assigning genomes to GTDB species clusters FROM 0.65 TO 0.5 starting in the next GTDB release IN ORDER TO BETTER ACCOMMODATE THE GROWING NUMBER OF INCOMPLETE MAGs contained in the GTDB WHICH CAN CAUSE THE AF BETWEEN MAGS TO BE ARTIFICIALLY LOW.` **The membership rule is loosened because the evidence got worse, not because the organisms changed** - and the sentence says so
span.quote: Related to MAG quality, we expect to change the AF criteria used for assigning genomes to GTDB species clusters from 0.65 to 0.5 starting in the next GTDB release in order to better accommodate the growing number of incomplete MAGs contained in the GTDB which can cause the AF between MAGs to be artificially low.

span.label: AND DISCRETENESS IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: `2.2% CAN BE DESCRIBED AS FUZZY as they have one or more genomes with an interspecific ANI value >=95% AND 89.5% CAN BE DESCRIBED AS DISCRETE as they contain no genomes with an interspecific ANI value >94% ... but THIS RESULT SHOULD BE INTERPRETED WITH CARE AS MOST BACTERIAL AND ARCHAEAL SPECIES LACK GENOMIC REPRESENTATION.` **The clusters are mostly clean; the boundary between them is not a gap in nature** - both are true, and the paper keeps both
span.quote: In terms of species, 2.2% can be described as fuzzy as they have one or more genomes with an interspecific ANI value ≥95% and 89.5% can be described as discrete as they contain no genomes with an interspecific ANI value >94% (Figure 4F ). Encouragingly, this indicates that GTDB species clusters are largely discrete, but this result should be interpreted with care as most bacterial and archaeal species lack genomic representation based on even conservative estimates of the number of prokaryotic species in nature ( 36 ).

span.label: **THE SPECIES DEFINITION IS ADMITTED TO HAVE NO NATURAL BOUNDARY BEHIND IT**: `The use of ANI to delineate species DESPITE THE LACK OF CLEAR EVIDENCE FOR DISCRETE SPECIES BOUNDARIES in the GTDB dataset IS A PRAGMATIC APPROACH.` This is a stronger disclosure than most definitional papers make - **the authors ran the test that would have vindicated their own threshold and published the negative result**
span.quote: The use of ANI to delineate species despite the lack of clear evidence for discrete species boundaries in the GTDB dataset is a pragmatic approach for organizing the rapidly growing biodiversity being discovered with metagenomic approaches ( 2 , 3 , 15 ). Leaving this diversity unclassified would severely limit the ability to effectively communicate scientific results as exemplified by 28.5% of genomes at NCBI lacking a species classification and 77.0% of GTDB R06-RS202 species clusters having an alphanumeric placeholder name.

span.label: AND THE DISCRETENESS RESULT IS BOUNDED BY WHAT HAS BEEN SEQUENCED: `this result SHOULD BE INTERPRETED WITH CARE AS MOST BACTERIAL AND ARCHAEAL SPECIES LACK GENOMIC REPRESENTATION BASED ON EVEN CONSERVATIVE ESTIMATES of the number of prokaryotic species in nature.` **The clusters look discrete partly because the space between them has not been sampled**
span.quote: In terms of species, 2.2% can be described as fuzzy as they have one or more genomes with an interspecific ANI value ≥95% and 89.5% can be described as discrete as they contain no genomes with an interspecific ANI value >94% (Figure 4F ). Encouragingly, this indicates that GTDB species clusters are largely discrete, but this result should be interpreted with care as most bacterial and archaeal species lack genomic representation based on even conservative estimates of the number of prokaryotic species in nature ( 36 ).

span.label: AND HALF THE TAXA HAVE NEVER BEEN GROWN: `OVER 70% OF ARCHAEAL SPECIES, GENERA, FAMILIES, AND ORDERS LACKING AN AVAILABLE CULTURED REPRESENTATIVE`, and over 50% of bacterial taxa `CONSIST EXCLUSIVELY OF MAGs AND/OR SAGs` although those are only 20.2% of the genomes. **A taxonomy of organisms nobody has in a flask**
span.quote: Unlike the number of bacterial genomes, MAGs account for the majority of taxonomic diversity covered by GTDB R06-RS202 (Figure 1E and F ; Supplementary Table S1 ). Over 50% of bacterial taxa, regardless of rank, consist exclusively of MAGs and/or SAGs despite MAGs (50 669 genomes) and SAGs (745 genomes) representing only 20.2% of the 254 090 bacterial genomes. Similarly, nearly 50% of all archaeal taxa, regardless of rank, consist exclusively of MAGs and/or SAGs with over 70% of archaeal species, genera, families, and orders lacking an available cultured representative (Figure 1F ).

span.label: AND THE DISCRETENESS ANALYSIS TAKES TWO SHORTCUTS, BOTH NAMED: `IT WAS ASSUMED THAT IF THE CLOSEST GTDB REPRESENTATIVE GENOME FOR SPECIES A WAS FOUND TO BE SPECIES B, THAT THE CLOSEST GENOME FOR ANY GENOME IN SPECIES A WILL BE IN SPECIES B. Furthermore, for the 87 SPECIES CONTAINING >150 GENOMES ONLY A RANDOMLY SELECTED SUBSET OF 150 GENOMES WAS CONSIDERED.` Declared in the Methods, and both would move the fuzzy/discrete split in the same direction - toward discreteness
span.quote: In order to reduce computational requirements, it was assumed that if the closest GTDB representative genome for species A was found to be species B, that the closest genome for any genome in species A will be in species B. Furthermore, for the 87 species containing >150 genomes only a randomly selected subset of 150 genomes was considered though these were compared to all genomes in species B regardless of the number of genomes in this species.

span.label: AND THE TYPE MATERIAL ITSELF IS NOT ALWAYS KNOWABLE: `ESTABLISHING THE PROVENANCE OF TYPE MATERIAL REMAINS AN ONGOING CHALLENGE and this decision is made by considering a number of factors including the classification of 16S rRNA genes ..., the type status of genomes at NCBI, PREVIOUS GTDB CLASSIFICATIONS, consideration of all pairwise ANI values AND LITERATURE REVIEW.` **One of the inputs to the decision is the database's own previous answer**
span.quote: Establishing the provenance of type material remains an ongoing challenge and this decision is made by considering a number of factors including the classification of 16S rRNA genes against the Living Tree Project database ( 13 ), the type status of genomes at NCBI, previous GTDB classifications, consideration of all pairwise ANI values and literature review.

span.note: eliminates: the objection that the missing discontinuity is an artefact of how GTDB picks species representatives · outcome: held
span.quote: This lack of a genetic discontinuity also persists when considering only genomes assembled from the type strain of a species, indicating that this result is independent of the methodology used to select GTDB species representatives (Figure 4B ).

span.label: requiring a Balanced ANI Score at least 10 above the incumbent before a species representative may be replaced
span.note: eliminates: a name drifting to a different genome every release as new assemblies arrive · outcome: held

span.label: refusing Latin names without an associated publication, without designated type material, or published only as a preprint
span.note: eliminates: names that cannot be anchored to a genome, and names that change between preprint and publication · outcome: held
span.quote: Effectively published Latin names above the rank of genus without designated type material, either a sequenced type strain or MAG, will no longer be incorporated into GTDB, and those that do will only be introduced when the associated type genome is present in GTDB. This change is necessary as establishing the correct interior node in the reference tree for taxa without type material can be ambiguous, particularly when the addition of new genomes or alternative inference methods results in the named taxon becoming polyphyletic in later releases.

span.label: never replacing an alphanumeric placeholder with another placeholder, however unwieldy
span.note: eliminates: breaking the link between a published result and the taxon it named · outcome: held
span.quote: Finally, to preserve name continuity, we do not replace alphanumeric placeholder names with other placeholder names, even when names (mostly introduced in early releases) are unwieldy, e.g. CG2-30-70-394 which is used as a genus, family, order, class and phylum name.

span.label: `Balanced ANI Score` - `0.5 x (ANI score) + 0.5 x (quality score)`, the rule deciding when the genome a species name points at may be swapped
span.quote: GTDB representatives are updated according to two primary principles: (i) representatives should be assembled from the type strain of a species whenever possible, and (ii) representatives should only be replaced by equivalent assemblies of demonstrably higher quality (Figure 3B ). These two principles are quantitatively defined by the Balanced ANI Score (BAS) which is 0.5 × (ANI score) + 0.5 × (quality score), where the ANI score is 100 – 20 × (100 – ANI to current representative) and the quality score is defined by the criteria given in Table 1 . span.label: the second membership criterion, and the one about to move from 0.65 to 0.5 because incomplete MAGs depress it
span.quote: Related to MAG quality, we expect to change the AF criteria used for assigning genomes to GTDB species clusters from 0.65 to 0.5 starting in the next GTDB release in order to better accommodate the growing number of incomplete MAGs contained in the GTDB which can cause the AF between MAGs to be artificially low.

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkab776.
